question: In her 2025 State of the Union address before Parliament, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the Commission’s intention to present a legal initiative on short-term rentals (STRs), with the stated objective of tackling the persistent regulatory gaps and challenges in this fast-growing sector.
The current, highly fragmented regulatory framework is insufficient to address the offline, local impacts of STRs and to regulate the functioning of the market and relevant platforms.

Given the significant implications of STR platforms for urban planning, the housing market and the affordability of housing for families across the Union, further clarification is needed regarding the scope and timing of this initiative. Can the Commission clarify: 1.
the type of legislative initiative envisaged and indicate an expected timeline for its presentation?
whether it has carried out an assessment of the link between STRs, families’ access to affordable housing and developments in the EU property market?
whether it has compiled a comprehensive map of the STR situation in EU cities?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.11.2025) The European Affordable Housing Plan will be accompanied by an analysis1 of key factors influencing the lack of affordable housing across the EU, including the impact of short-term accommodation rentals on the property and rental markets, in particular in highly touristic destinations.

An assessment on the form and content of any initiative will likely follow in the course of 2026, including on the basis of the data that will be generated via the Short-term rentals Regulation2, which will be applicable from May 2026. The timing is indicated in the Commission Work Programme3 and will be referred in by European Affordable Housing Plan.
1 In form of a Commission Staff Working Document. 2 Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 April 2024 on data collection

and sharing relating to short-term accommodation rental services, OJ L, 2024/1028, 29.4.2024,https://eurlex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1028/oj/eng. 3 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52025DC0870.
